subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Nebulae: Stellar Nurseries
description: A 60-second lesson on Nebulae: Stellar Nurseries.

hook.text: Stars are born inside vast clouds of gas and dust called nebulae. Some nurseries span hundreds of light-years.

buildup.text: Gravity pulls pockets of gas together. As the clump shrinks, it heats up. A protostar begins to glow.

discovery.text: The Orion Nebula is the closest major star nursery—1,344 light-years away and visible to the naked eye.

twist.text: A single nebula can birth thousands of stars at once. They form in clusters, not in isolation.

climax.text: The James Webb Telescope revealed newborn stars still wrapped in cocoons of dust inside distant nebulae.

punchline.text: Every star began as a collapsing cloud. Including ours.

quiz.question: What triggers a star to begin forming inside a nebula?
options: Gravity pulls gas together, heating it into a protostar
Lightning strikes inside the cloud ignite hydrogen fusion
Solar wind from nearby stars pushes gas into a ball

details.summary: Nebulae are vast clouds of gas and dust where stars are born. Gravity causes regions within these clouds to collapse, heating up until nuclear fusion ignites a new star. The most famous stellar nursery, the Orion Nebula, is visible to the naked eye and actively forming new stars today.
details.whyItMatters: Nebulae connect stellar death to stellar birth — they're made from material ejected by previous generations of stars. Understanding nebulae reveals how the universe recycles matter to create new solar systems.
takeaways: Nebulae are gas and dust clouds where stars form
Gravity collapses regions until fusion ignites a new star
The Orion Nebula is a famous active stellar nursery

faq.question: What triggers star formation in a nebula?
faq.answer: Shockwaves from nearby supernovae, collisions between gas clouds, or density waves from spiral arms compress regions of the nebula. Once compressed past a critical density, gravity overcomes gas pressure and collapse becomes self-sustaining, eventually forming protostars.

faq.question: Are all nebulae stellar nurseries?
faq.answer: No. Emission nebulae and dark nebulae are star-forming regions, but planetary nebulae are shells ejected by dying stars, and supernova remnants are debris from stellar explosions. The term nebula simply means a diffuse cloud of gas and dust in space.
